Actual Article Body:
Your digital subscription includes access to content from all our websites in your region.
Access unlimited news content and The Canberra Times app. Premium subscribers also enjoy interactive puzzles and access to the digital version of our print edition - Today's Paper.

A fraudster who stole more than $40,000 from Services Australia told a report author his crimes were "a joke or a prank".

Login or signup to continue reading

Ali Al Kinani's crimes "fundamentally harm a social welfare system designed for those in financial hardship," Justice Jon White said on Friday, November 13.

Al Kinani, 37, was handed a two-year-and-eight-month jail sentence in the ACT Supreme Court.

He will be released on a recognisance order in March 2028, after one year and four months behind bars.

The fraudster has also been ordered to pay the money back to the Commonwealth of Australia.

He previously pleaded guilty to a rolled-up count of obtaining financial advantage by deception and using a forged document to influence a Commonwealth official.

Between July 2020 and February 2023, Al Kinani compromised the Services Australia records of four people to fraudulently obtain a total of $40,371.

He did so by lodging false claims for emergency payments in their names and redirecting the funds to his bank accounts.

Because of the redirections, some of the victims also did not receive their regular payments.

As part of his crimes, Al Kinani lodged claims for JobSeeker, coronavirus, tax benefit and carer payments.

In doing so he uploaded identity documents in the names of his victims including passports and bank cards.

Al Kinani also called Services Australia and pretended to be the account holder, giving his own home address and phone number in response to questions.

On January 4, 2024, he visited the Services Australia branch in Gungahlin purporting to be a man who had recently been released from jail in NSW.

He returned a few days later with a prison release certificate, dated December 29, 2023, in the other man's name.

Staff at Services Australia had concerns about the document and when they contacted Corrective Services NSW they discovered the named man remained incarcerated.

Al Kinani was arrested for unrelated fraud and money laundering in January 2024 after stealing an eftpos machine and using it to steal more than $16,568 via unauthorised refunds, and attempting to obtain a further $55,651.

He was handed an almost two-year jail sentence for the eftpos fraud...
